intro: Age problems describe people’s ages now, some years ago and some years from now. Call the age you don’t know x, write every other age from it (x − 5 five years ago, x + 15 in fifteen years), turn the sentence into an equation and solve it.

tips.title: Call the unknown age x
tips.body: Pick the age you don’t know and call it x. Every other age, past or future, is x plus or minus some years. Then write the sentence as an equation.
tips.caption: Ram now: x. Five years ago: x − 5. In 15 years: x + 15. So x + 15 = 5(x − 5), and x = 10.

tips.title: Everyone ages the same
tips.body: In t years, every person is t years older. So the difference between two ages never changes, while the sum of two ages grows by 2t.

tips.title: Ratios of ages
tips.body: For a ratio of 5 : 6, write the ages as 5k and 6k. Add (or take away) the years from both, set the new ratio and cross-multiply: (5k + 6) × 8 = (6k + 6) × 7, so k = 3 and the ages are 15 and 18.

tips.title: Check with the options
tips.body: Put your answer back into every sentence of the question. Ages must be whole numbers that make sense: a father is older than his son, and nobody’s age goes below 0.
